stanzas.sanskrit:
इन्द्रद्युम्नः पाण्ड्यखण्डाधिराज-
-स्त्वद्भक्तात्मा चन्दनाद्रौ कदाचित् ।
त्वत्सेवायां मग्नधीरालुलोके
नैवागस्त्यं प्राप्तमातिथ्यकामम् ॥ २६-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Indradyumna, the king of Paandya land & Bhagwan’s great devotee was once engrossed in worshipping Bhagwan on the Malaya mountain. He was so absorbed that he did not even notice sage Agastya who approached expecting his hospitality.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
indradyumnaḥ pāṇḍyakhaṇḍādhirāja-
-stvadbhaktātmā candanādrau kadācit |
tvatsevāyāṁ magnadhīrāluloke
naivāgastyaṁ prāptamātithyakāmam || 26-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कुम्भोद्भूतिः सम्भृतक्रोधभारः
स्तब्धात्मा त्वं हस्तिभूयं भजेति ।
शप्त्वाऽथैनं प्रत्यगात् सोऽपि लेभे
हस्तीन्द्रत्वं त्वत्स्मृतिव्यक्तिधन्यम् ॥ २६-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Agastya who was so angry cursed the king to be born as an elephant and departed. Indradyumna got the form of a lordly elephant with the good fortune of retaining a clear memory of Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kumbhodbhūtiḥ sambhṛtakrodhabhāraḥ
stabdhātmā tvaṁ hastibhūyaṁ bhajeti |
śaptvā’thainaṁ pratyagāt so’pi lebhe
hastīndratvaṁ tvatsmṛtivyaktidhanyam || 26-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
दुग्धाम्भोधेर्मध्यभाजि त्रिकूटे
क्रीडन् शैले यूथपोऽयं वशाभिः ।
सर्वान् जन्तूनत्यवर्तिष्ट शक्त्या
त्वद्भक्तानां कुत्र नोत्कर्षलाभः ॥ २६-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Indradyumna became the leader of elephants, now known as Gajendra, played with female elephants on the Trikoota mountains and was living happily.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dugdhāmbhodhermadhyabhāji trikūṭe
krīḍan śaile yūthapo’yaṁ vaśābhiḥ |
sarvān jantūnatyavartiṣṭa śaktyā
tvadbhaktānāṁ kutra notkarṣalābhaḥ || 26-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
स्वेन स्थेम्ना दिव्यदेशत्वशक्त्या
सोऽयं खेदानप्रजानन् कदाचित् ।
शैलप्रान्ते घर्मतान्तः सरस्यां
यूथैः सार्धं त्वत्प्रणुन्नोऽभिरेमे ॥ २६-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: One day Gajendra while roaming in the mountains, felt thirsty due to heat and went to a lake nearby, to drink water along with his female elephants.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
svena sthemnā divyadeśatvaśaktyā
so’yaṁ khedānaprajānan kadācit |
śailaprānte gharmatāntaḥ sarasyāṁ
yūthaiḥ sārdhaṁ tvatpraṇunno’bhireme || 26-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
हूहूस्तावद्देवलस्यापि शापा-
-द्ग्राहीभूतस्तज्जले वर्तमानः ।
जग्राहैनं हस्तिनं पाददेशे
शान्त्यर्थं हि श्रान्तिदोऽसि स्वकानाम् ॥ २६-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: In that lake, there was a gandarva named Huhu, who had turned in to a crocodile, cursed by sage Devala. He caught the leg of Gajendra. Indeed Bhagwan gives difficulties to his devotees, only to bless later.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hūhūstāvaddevalasyāpi śāpā-
-dgrāhībhūtastajjale vartamānaḥ |
jagrāhainaṁ hastinaṁ pādadeśe
śāntyarthaṁ hi śrāntido’si svakānām || 26-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वत्सेवाया वैभवाद्दुर्निरोधं
युद्ध्यन्तं तं वत्सराणां सहस्रम् ।
प्राप्ते काले त्वत्पदैकाग्र्यसिद्ध्यै
नक्राक्रान्तं हस्तिवर्यं व्यधास्त्वम् ॥ २६-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gajendra fought with all his might for more than thousand years but still crocodile did not leave him. When the time for his redemption had come, he was fit for one-pointed devotion to Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvatsevāyā vaibhavāddurnirodhaṁ
yuddhyantaṁ taṁ vatsarāṇāṁ sahasram |
prāpte kāle tvatpadaikāgryasiddhyai
nakrākrāntaṁ hastivaryaṁ vyadhāstvam || 26-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
आर्तिव्यक्तप्राक्तनज्ञानभक्तिः
शुण्डोत् क्षिप्तैः पुण्डरीकैः समर्चन् ।
पूर्वाभ्यस्तं निर्विशेषात्मनिष्ठं
स्तोत्रश्रेष्ठं सोऽन्वगादीत् परात्मन् ॥ २६-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The time Gajendra became tired, he started singing hymns in praise of Bhagwan which he had learnt in his past life. He plucked the white lotus in the lake and offered it to the Lord.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ārtivyaktaprāktanajñānabhaktiḥ
śuṇḍot kṣiptaiḥ puṇḍarīkaiḥ samarcan |
pūrvābhyastaṁ nirviśeṣātmaniṣṭhaṁ
stotraśreṣṭhaṁ so’nvagādīt parātman || 26-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा स्तोत्रं निर्गुणस्थं समस्तं
ब्रह्मेशाद्यैर्नाहमित्यप्रयाते ।
सर्वात्मा त्वं भूरिकारुण्यवेगात्
तार्क्ष्यारूढः प्रेक्षितोऽभूः पुरस्तात् ॥ २६-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: On hearing the hymns, Brahma and Shiva did not proceed to help as the sloka was addressed to Bhagwan Hari . Lord immediately in his unlimited mercy, mounted on Garuda and appeared before Gajendra.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śrutvā stotraṁ nirguṇasthaṁ samastaṁ
brahmeśādyairnāhamityaprayāte |
sarvātmā tvaṁ bhūrikāruṇyavegāt
tārkṣyārūḍhaḥ prekṣito’bhūḥ purastāt || 26-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
हस्तीन्द्रं तं हस्तपद्मेन धृत्वा
चक्रेण त्वं नक्रवर्यं व्यदारीः ।
गन्धर्वेऽस्मिन् मुक्तशापे स हस्ती
त्वत्सारूप्यं प्राप्य देदीप्यते स्म ॥ २६-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Lord held Gajendra with his lotus hands and released him from the clutches of the crocodile by severing with Bhagwan’s discus.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hastīndraṁ taṁ hastapadmena dhṛtvā
cakreṇa tvaṁ nakravaryaṁ vyadārīḥ |
gandharve’smin muktaśāpe sa hastī
tvatsārūpyaṁ prāpya dedīpyate sma || 26-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
एतद्वृत्तं त्वां च मां च प्रगे यो
गायेत् सोऽयं भूयसे श्रेयसे स्यात् ।
इत्युक्त्वैनं तेन सार्धं गतस्त्वं
धिष्ण्यं विष्णो पाहि वातालयेश ॥ २६-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan departed to Vaikunta along with Gajendra after giving the benefits of reading or singing or hearing the Gajendra moksham. Bhattathiri requests Lord who saved Gajendra from jaws of death and blessed him, to protect all devotees including him in the same way.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
etadvṛttaṁ tvāṁ ca māṁ ca prage yo
gāyet so’yaṁ bhūyase śreyase syāt |
ityuktvainaṁ tena sārdhaṁ gatastvaṁ
dhiṣṇyaṁ viṣṇo pāhi vātālayeśa || 26-10 ||
